newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel gains on dollar, Bank of Israel intervenes.
newsitem.headline: Shekel gains on dollar, Bank of Israel intervenes.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Tuesday in active trading even as the central bank intervened heavily to support the currency basket, dealers said.

"The business sector was selling dollars today on a relatively high scale, pushing the basket below the lower edge of its trading band. The Bank of Israel had to buy more than $200 million to support the basket," said a dealer at Bank Leumi.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the basket of foreign currencies, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.
"Investors are waiting to see if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time in two years," the dealer said.
Dealers noted that the dollar's price reflects expectations for a 25-basis-point rate increase.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3660 shekels against 3.3720 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6574 shekels against 3.6571 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7245 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7336 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9959 shekels after 1.9936 on Friday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3650 shekels.
